reviews.body:
Thanks for the fix and the detailed write-up, @pcbeingused333, and for the quick follow-ups on index ordering and key resolution. I reproduced #8994 on main and confirmed the branch keeps the tool calls and reasoning for Groq, Together and Cerebras.

1. `cerebras/chat_completion_chunks_aggregator.py:60` and `groq/chat_completion_chunks_aggregator.py:60` read `delta.tool_calls` directly, while `reasoning` uses `getattr` because the SDKs are unpinned. On a version without that attribute, the blanket `except` in `aggregate()` drops the whole span output. Please use `getattr(delta, "tool_calls", None) or []`.
2. Tests: compare the whole aggregated message to a fully built expected one instead of `message["tool_calls"]` plus `not in` checks, so a wrong `content`, `role` or `finish_reason` is caught too.

Minor:
- `StreamedToolCalls` is now a third copy of the merge logic. OpenAI's aggregator could use it directly and drop `_merge_tool_call` (Mistral can stay, its `index` defaults to `0`).
- A tool-call version of `test_together_chat_completions_create__stream__happyflow` (respx + `assert_equal`) would cover the SSE parsing and span output end to end.
- `_FloatIndexToolCall` could be Together's real `together.types.tool_choice.ToolChoice`, so the test follows the SDK.
- Heads-up: #8239 also touches the Cerebras aggregator and tests, so whichever lands second needs a rebase; yours uses `message["reasoning"]`, which matches Together on main.

Thanks again for working through the streaming integrations!

Thanks for the fix and the detailed write-up, @pcbeingused333. The logic looks right to me. I reproduced #8994 on main and confirmed the branch keeps the tool calls and reasoning for Groq, Together and Cerebras. A few nits:

1. nit: `StreamedToolCalls` is now a third copy of the merge logic, after `_merge_tool_call` in `openai/chat_completion_chunks_aggregator.py` and the one in the Mistral aggregator. OpenAI's tool-call `index` is always an int, so its aggregator could use the helper directly and drop its private copy. Mistral can stay as it is, since its SDK defaults a missing `index` to `0`.
2. nit: the new aggregator tests check `message["tool_calls"]` plus `"... not in message"`. Comparing the whole aggregated object to a fully built expected one would also catch a wrong `content`, `role` or `finish_reason`.
3. nit: `test_together.py` already drives a real stream through `create(stream=True)` with respx and checks the trace tree with `assert_equal` (`test_together_chat_completions_create__stream__happyflow`). A tool-call version of that test would cover the SSE parsing and the span output end to end, not just `aggregate()`.
4. nit: `_FloatIndexToolCall` in `test_streamed_tool_calls.py` could be Together's real `together.types.tool_choice.ToolChoice` (its `index` is a `float`), so the test follows any change in the SDK.

Thanks again for the contribution!

Thanks for the review. Pushed c1d681d08d on top of the branch.

1. `delta.tool_calls` is now read with `getattr(delta, "tool_calls", None) or []` in the Groq and Cerebras aggregators, and in the Together one for parity. Groq and Cerebras each got a test with a delta that has no `tool_calls` attribute; it raised `AttributeError` before and now keeps the content.
2. Understood on the overlap with #8239. The Cerebras reasoning here is stored under `message["reasoning"]`, the same key the Together aggregator on main uses, so the SDK team can pick the order and whoever lands second adjusts the key.

Nits:
- 2: the tool-call aggregator tests for Groq, Cerebras and Together now compare the whole choice (role, content, finish reason and tool calls).
- 3: added a Together test that drives a tool-call stream through `create(stream=True)` with respx and checks the span output.
- 4: the float-index unit test now builds its fragments from `together.types.tool_choice.ToolChoice` (via `model_construct`, since a continuation fragment lacks most of the required fields) instead of the local stand-in class.
- 1: not changed in this PR. Moving the OpenAI aggregator onto `StreamedToolCalls` touches a different integration, so it is better as a separate change if wanted.

The updated Groq, Cerebras and Together aggregator tests and the helper unit tests pass locally; the Groq end-to-end tests that need a Groq key were not run.

Merger   🟠 Needs Review

 Not ready to merge: PR has unresolved findings that need to be addressed.

Done in 42227bd: `_streamed_tool_calls.py` now lives in each of the groq, together and cerebras packages (duplicated as discussed), the aggregators import it from their own package, and the unit test is split per package. The OpenAI aggregator is untouched.

Tests: unit/integrations for groq, together, cerebras and openai pass (23 passed).


This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Thanks for all the work on this, @pcbeingused333, and for the quick turnarounds on each round of feedback. We're almost there to merge this.

A couple of last things:

1. **Please rebase on `main`.** The Together integration changed there in #9202 (support for together 3.x). `BASE_URL` was removed from `test_together.py`, so the new streamed tool-call test fails lint on the merged code (`F821 Undefined name BASE_URL`). Please adapt the test to the new setup and re-run the Together tests after the rebase.
2. **Please go through the open Baz comments** and either apply the suggestion or reply with why not.

Thanks again!

Merged current `main` into the branch (instead of rebasing, to keep the review history) and adapted the Together streamed tool-call test: `BASE_URL` is gone, so it now uses `@respx.mock()` + `post(path=COMPLETIONS_ROUTE)` like the rest of the file (7e074fe). Together tests re-run on together 3.x: 25 passed with the groq/cerebras streamed tool-call tests, ruff check/format clean.

Baz: the unit-test import comment no longer applies (those tests live under `tests/library_integration`, where the provider SDKs are installed); the `index` comment is corrected in the groq, together and cerebras helpers.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
Thanks for the clarification and updates.
